```{r setup}
library(adorn)
```

These examples use the `timed`, `logged` and `memoize` decorators from
`vignette("writing-decorators")`, repeated here so this vignette stands alone. The
`memoize` here is a minimal version that keys on the raw arguments and needs no
other packages; `vignette("writing-decorators")` has a fuller one.

```{r timed}
timed <- decorator(
  function(f, ..., digits = 3) {
    name <- decorator_context()$name
    start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
    on.exit(message(sprintf(
      "%s took %s s",
      name,
      round(proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - start, digits)
    )))
    f(...)
  },
  name = "timed"
)
```

```{r logged}
logged <- decorator(
  function(f, ...) {
    name <- decorator_context()$name
    message("-> ", name)
    result <- withVisible(f(...))
    message("<- ", name)
    if (result$visible) result$value else invisible(result$value)
  },
  name = "logged"
)
```

```{r memoize}
memoize <- decorator(
  function(f) {
    cache <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
    function(...) {
      key <- paste(deparse(list(...)), collapse = "")
      if (!exists(key, envir = cache, inherits = FALSE)) {
        assign(key, f(...), envir = cache)
      }
      get(key, envir = cache, inherits = FALSE)
    }
  },
  name = "memoize"
)
```

# Defining a method

`%@%` works wherever you define a function, so it can decorate a method as you
write it.

## S3

```{r s3}
money <- function(x) structure(list(amount = x), class = "money")

print.money <- logged %@%
  function(x, ...) {
    cat("$", format(x$amount, nsmall = 2), "\n")
    invisible(x)
  }

print(money(12.5))
```

## S4

```{r s4}
setClass("Circle", representation(r = "numeric"))
setGeneric("area", function(shape, ...) standardGeneric("area"))

setMethod("area", "Circle", logged %@% function(shape, ...) pi * shape@r^2)

area(new("Circle", r = 2))
```

## S7

```{r s7}
library(S7)

Dog := new_class("Dog", properties = list(name = class_character))

speak := new_generic("speak", "x")
method(speak, Dog) <- logged %@% function(x) paste(x@name, "says woof")

speak(Dog(name = "Rex"))
```

## R6

Decorated methods keep access to `self` and `private`, and `invisible(self)`
still chains.

```{r r6, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
library(R6)

Counter <- R6Class(
  "Counter",
  public = list(
    n = 0,
    add = logged %@%
      function(k = 1) {
        self$n <- self$n + k
        invisible(self)
      }
  )
)

counter <- Counter$new()
counter$add(2)$add(3)
counter$n
```

A stateful decorator works too. R6 methods belong to the class, so the cache
below is shared by every `Model` object (the key is the argument, not `self`).

```{r r6-memoize, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
Model <- R6Class(
  "Model",
  public = list(
    scale = 10,
    predict = memoize %@%
      function(x) {
        message("computing")
        x * self$scale
      }
  )
)

m <- Model$new()
m$predict(2)
m$predict(2)
```

# Decorating a method that already exists

`%@%` is for methods you are defining. When the class is already built, perhaps
by another package, use `decorate()` to wrap one of its methods afterwards.
Each call adds a layer on the outside, and `decorators()` lists the stack,
outermost first.

## S3

Give `decorate()` the generic's name as a string and the class. This works for
any generic.

```{r s3-decorate}
format.money <- function(x, ...) paste0("$", x$amount)
decorate("format", timed, class = "money")

format(money(3))
```

You can also pass the generic function itself with the replacement form, as for
the other systems. The generic must call `UseMethod()` directly, so internal
generics such as `length()` need the string form above.

```{r s3-replace}
perimeter <- function(x, ...) UseMethod("perimeter")
perimeter.square <- function(x, ...) 4 * x$side

decorate(perimeter, "square") <- logged

perimeter(structure(list(side = 3), class = "square"))
```

## S4

Give `decorate()` the generic and the signature.

```{r s4-decorate}
setClass("Square", representation(side = "numeric"))
setMethod("area", "Square", function(shape, ...) shape@side^2)

decorate(area, logged, signature = "Square")
decorate(area, timed, signature = "Square")

area(new("Square", side = 3))
decorators(getMethod("area", "Square"))
```

The replacement form works here too, and mirrors S7's `method(generic, class) <- fn`:

```{r s4-replace}
decorate(area, "Square") <- logged

area(new("Square", side = 3))
```

## S7

Give `decorate()` the generic and the class. The method is wrapped in place.

```{r s7-decorate}
decorate(speak, timed, class = Dog)

speak(Dog(name = "Rex"))
```

The stack can be inspected, and the replacement form mirrors
`method(generic, class) <- fn`:

```{r s7-replace}
decorate(speak, Dog) <- memoize

decorators(method(speak, Dog))
```

`undecorate()` returns the original function. Register it again to remove all
the decorators.

```{r s7-undecorate}
method(speak, Dog) <- undecorate(method(speak, Dog))

speak(Dog(name = "Rex"))
```

## R6

Give `decorate()` the name of the method and the class generator as `class`,
the same shape as for S3. Objects
created afterwards use the decorated method; objects that already exist keep
the old one, because R6 copies methods into each object when it is created.

```{r r6-decorate, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
Resetter <- R6Class(
  "Resetter",
  public = list(
    n = 0,
    add = function(k = 1) {
      self$n <- self$n + k
      invisible(self)
    },
    reset = function() {
      self$n <- 0
      invisible(self)
    }
  )
)

decorate("add", logged, class = Resetter)

r <- Resetter$new()
r$add(2)$add(3)
r$n
```

Pass several names to decorate several methods at once. Use `where` for methods that are not public
(`"public"` is the default, the others are `"private"` and `"active"`).

```{r r6-where, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
Safe <- R6Class(
  "Safe",
  public = list(go = function() private$step()),
  private = list(step = function() "ok")
)

decorate("step", logged, class = Safe, where = "private")
Safe$new()$go()
```

A method the class only inherits is copied into the class you pass and
decorated there. The parent is not changed, as with S7. The copy is a
snapshot: decorating the parent again later does not affect it.

```{r r6-inherit, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
Doubler <- R6Class("Doubler", inherit = Resetter)

decorate("reset", timed, class = Doubler)

invisible(Doubler$new()$reset()) # timed
invisible(Resetter$new()$reset()) # not timed
```

For public methods the replacement form also works, and takes the same shape as
S7's `method(generic, class) <- fn`.

```{r r6-replace, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
decorate(Resetter, "reset") <- logged

invisible(Resetter$new()$reset())
```
